extraction.NOTES: Document is a partially legible printed application form (Form 5-105, Act of May 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 182; form number 6-2543) for a patent in fee. Handwritten responses are largely illegible. Degree of blood appears to be '24' (possibly 1/4). The application appears to cover allotment No. [illegible] and references 1929. Most answers to the 27 questions are either blank or illegible. The document is notarized but the notary, date, and applicant name/signature are not legible.

tables.title: Application for Patent in Fee - Anna Shuck Questionnaire Responses

rows.Question: Age?
Degree of blood?
Married or single?
Did you attend school? If so, where and how long?
rows.Answer: 5 yrs Stephan Indian Mission Hyde Co. SD; 2 yrs Chamberlain SD

rows.Question: Do you use intoxicants?
Are you in good physical condition?
What is the value of the land covered by your application?
Does your application cover your own allotment or inherited land?
Does your application cover all or a part of your land?
Do you cultivate your land?
Have you any other occupation?
Are you self-supporting? If so, how is your self-support obtained?
Have you accumulated any property? If so, what?
rows.Answer: 80 acres of land, horses and cattle, also farming implements

rows.Question: Are you in debt? If so, whom do you owe, how much, and for what, and have you given security for the debts?
Have you been given a patent in fee for a part of your land? If so, did you sell it, and what use did you make of the proceeds of the sale?
Have you any inherited land? If so, what is your interest in the estate and what is the value of the allotment?
Have you sold any inherited land? If so, what use was made of the proceeds?
Have you any individual Indian money to your credit with the superintendent? If so, how much?
Have you been given the privilege of leasing your own land?
Is your land leased? If so, what rent do you receive?
rows.Answer: I am using my own land

rows.Question: What price?
Has anyone asked you to procure a patent in fee for the purpose of disposing of your land?
Have other members of your family allotments of their own? If so, give names, sex, ages, relationship, and number of acres, and approximate value of each allotment.
rows.Answer: Two daughters: Aeda Bell Shuck age 14 yrs. 160 acres value $3,000; Caroline Alice Shuck age 8 yrs. 160 acres value $3,000

rows.Question: What members of your family, if any, have no allotment? Designate those dependent on you for support, and give reasons, stating ages and sex.
What practical business experience have you had?
Have you other lands that would continue to be held in trust after the lands described in this application are released? If so, give acreage, value, and character of improvements thereon.
Set forth fully your reasons for requesting a patent in fee.
rows.Answer: I want to borrow money to purchase other land and more cattle
